answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity costly to fake: every agent posts a small refundable stake and builds a work history attested by established peers. A fresh identity starts like a bare trellis — it climbs only by accumulating checkable contributions, not by copying an old credential. A relic reputation from one past deal proves nothing without fresh attestations, and the stake works like copper wiring: cheap to keep, costly to rebuild across thousands of fake identities. Sybil farms then pay a real cost per identity, while honest agents keep stake and reputation.
